problem: GitHub website validation could be green while Netlify production failed because pre-merge build parity did not fully match the production build environment.
root_cause: The parity job executed the same command chain but set STATIC_I18N_REQUIRE_CACHE=0 while netlify.toml production sets STATIC_I18N_REQUIRE_CACHE=1. A candidate could therefore pass CI under permissive cache behavior and fail in Netlify production.
prevention: Production parity must match both the Netlify build command and production-critical environment flags, including STATIC_I18N_REQUIRE_CACHE=1.
Every website candidate that requires preview must execute the exact Netlify production build chain before merge.
The parity job must include pricing-build-integrity capture and restore, apply-i18n, build-localized-routes, sitemap generation and release-evidence generation.
Production-like i18n environment values must be explicit in the parity job so build behavior is deterministic.
A green browser test built from a reduced composer is not sufficient evidence of Netlify buildability.
Terminal closure still requires exact production SHA and production browser proof after Netlify deployment.
